0-source-1.title: Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 of the European Parliament and of the Council on digital operational resilience for the financial sector (DORA)
0-source-1.applicability: All financial entities as defined in Article 3 (banks, insurance companies, investment firms, payment institutions etc.) and their critical ICT third-party service providers

passages.text: Financial entities should follow the same approach and the same principle-based rules when addressing ICT risk taking into account their size and overall risk profile, and the nature, scale and complexity of their services, activities and operations.

Likewise, financial entities should have policies in place for the testing of ICT systems, controls and processes, as well as for managing ICT third-party risk. The digital operational resilience baseline for financial entities should be increased while also allowing for a proportionate application of requirements for certain financial entities, particularly microenterprises, as well as financial entities subject to a simplified ICT risk management framework.

It is essential to harmonise the ICT-related incident reporting regime by requiring all financial entities to report to their competent authorities through a single streamlined framework as set out in this Regulation.

0-source-2.title: Digital operational resilience Regulation (DORA) | European Banking Authority
0-source-2.applicability: Official implementation guidance covering management body accountability (Article 5), simplified framework requirements (Article 16), and proportionality principles (Article 4)

passages.text: Article 16: Simplified ICT risk management framework

concerns.description: Determine financial entity category and scope under DORA Articles 1-3
Apply proportionality principle based on entity size, risk profile and complexity per Article 4
Establish management body accountability for ICT risk oversight and resource allocation per Article 5
Implement simplified ICT risk management framework for qualifying microenterprises per Article 16
